speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development in the last five years, what has been the annual number of single unwed mothers.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The 830 that was mentioned, which is the average number in the last five years, is she able to give the exact numbers in each of the last five years?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: What I am getting at is, is the number increasing or is the trend a decreasing one?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Second, regardless of the trend, 830 is still not a small number.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And as we know, many of us have spoken in this House, myself included, for both mother and children, that given their circumstances, they are disadvantaged in many ways.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I do recognise the many new benefits that we have extended to mother and children.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Are there gaps which are not currently addressed?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: While it may not be under MSF, it is an area of concern.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I do know that yes, we do look at it on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But I wonder whether a policy could be made to address the needs of these single unwed mothers.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: And beyond it, whether we could look at it from a whole-of-Government approach to deal with all challenges faced by this group of single unwed mothers and their children.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I will start off with the numbers first.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But this is a number that we monitor closely because we do agree with the Member that we want to ensure that we give as much support as we can to single unwed mothers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On his larger question about what we are doing, whole-of-Government, to support single unwed mothers, I would like to say that we hold a couple of principles.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: One I have mentioned in my main reply, which is that we have equalised the benefits for all citizen children.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have consistently been doing this in 2013, 2016, 2017, a whole range of updated measures to support citizen children.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There are some specific Government policies that are specific to the encouragement of parenthood within marriage.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, there are a few that are separate from the equalisation of all child benefits which I mentioned earlier.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Coming back to the main point of the question, which is what is our whole-of-Government approach towards supporting single unwed mothers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We also have Student Care Financial Assistance schemes to help these moms.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We also know that job support is important to them.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It is somewhat related to the earlier point I made about caregiving because if you build an ecosystem or support around their children, this frees up time for the mom to be able to look for a job.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There are, of course, job training as well as support grants to help these mothers re-enter the workforce.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Next, we also have specific programmes such as KidSTART which targets children in rental housing.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Some of them, they come from families where it is a single mom that is taking care of them.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have shared that we are scaling up the KidSTART programme.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Last but not least, sometimes our single unwed mothers also need counselling support and that is where the FSCs can come in.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I cannot answer on the Ministry of National Development's (MND's) behalf.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But from my last posting at MND, this was a topic that has been actively raised by Member Louis Ng before.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: MND has proactively removed impediments to single unweds when they try to apply for housing, for example, through the HDB online portal.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: HDB will assess whether or not the single unwed mother has family support, and in the instance where she does not have family support and she has a citizen child, then rest assured that HDB will ensure that she has housing options.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I think we can all agree: single unwed mothers do face a multitude of challenges, ranging from housing to caring for their children with limited resources.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: My question focuses on the children of single unwed mothers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I do not have the specific details of a research with me right now to address his question.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But given the long-standing work we have been doing with single unwed mothers and our understanding of the experience that they and their children have, I am quite sure that MSF has quite ample data to understand the impact that children can undergo or be impacted with when they grow up in such family situations.
